standard.title: Physical activity in natural settings
standard.description: participate in physical activities that enhance health and wellbeing in natural and outdoor settings, and analyse the steps and resources needed to promote participation
standard.prior_knowledge: At Years 3-4, students participated in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings to examine factors that can influence their own and others' participation (AC9HP4M05). They can identify participation barriers and enablers at a descriptive level but have not yet analysed the steps and resources needed to actively promote participation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings and analyse the steps and resources needed to promote participation for themselves and others.

nodes.label: Connecting outdoor activity to health and wellbeing
nodes.description: Explain how participation in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings specifically enhances health and wellbeing — distinguishing the contribution of the natural/outdoor context from physical activity in general.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in an outdoor physical activity and describe at least one way the natural or outdoor setting enhanced the health or wellbeing benefit beyond what an indoor activity would provide.
success_criteria: Identifies the specific contribution of the outdoor/natural context (not just that activity is good for health)
Can reference at least one dimension of wellbeing (physical, mental, social, or connection to place)
nodes.hinge_reason: The promotion analysis in N2 depends on understanding why outdoor participation matters — students who cannot articulate the outdoor-specific benefit will produce generic 'exercise is good' promotion strategies that don't address access or connection to natural environments.

response_modes.reason: Compare: same physical activity indoors vs outdoors — what changes? Connects lived experience of the activity to the health/wellbeing concept and builds the outdoor-specific rationale needed for N2.

nodes.label: Analysing access and participation factors
nodes.description: Identify and analyse the steps and resources needed to access and participate in outdoor physical activities — considering equity, environment, community and logistical factors.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two factors that influence access to or participation in an outdoor physical activity, and describe what steps or resources would help address one barrier.
success_criteria: Identifies both a barrier and an enabler (not just one type)
Proposes a concrete step or resource — not a vague 'we should encourage more people'
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Participation factors span community infrastructure, cultural connection (including First Nations connections to Country), physical environment, safety, and cost — each offers a distinct analytical angle.

response_modes.reason: Analyse participation factors for different natural settings and community contexts: a skate park, a bushwalking trail, a surf beach, a local park. The resource and step requirements differ across contexts, deepening analytical thinking.

nodes.label: Proposing promotion strategies
nodes.description: Propose strategies to promote participation in outdoor physical activities, drawing on the analysis of access factors and the health/wellbeing rationale.
nodes.minimum_width: Propose at least one strategy to increase participation in an outdoor physical activity, explaining the steps involved and the resources required.
success_criteria: Strategy addresses a specific identified barrier (not a general appeal)
Includes both steps (what to do) and resources (what is needed)

response_modes.reason: Integrates health/wellbeing rationale and access analysis into a promotion proposal — the full descriptor demand of 'analyse the steps and resources needed to promote participation'.
